editorial:
Imagine a movie that feels more like a collection of short stories about the messy side of love. You get three different tales that explore how people deal with desire and loneliness. First, you follow a couple in Tuscany who bring a younger woman into their relationship. Then, you meet a stressed-out ad boss who keeps having the same erotic dream while talking to his doctor. Finally, you travel back to the 1960s to see a high-class call girl who falls for her young tailor. It is a slow burn that focuses more on feelings and longing than big plot twists, making it feel like a dream you can't quite wake up from.

The acting is top-notch, especially in the period piece section which looks absolutely stunning. While some parts might feel too slow for you if you want a fast-paced romance, the visuals make up for it. If you enjoy movies that make you think about your own relationships, you will love this. The colors are so vivid that watching it in high definition is a must.
endingExplained: The final story wraps up with a sad look at love. The call girl and her tailor share a deep bond, but their social classes keep them apart. Even though they care for each other, they cannot find a way to be together in the real world. It ends on a quiet note, showing that some loves are just impossible. The movie closes by leaving you to wonder if desire is more about wanting someone than actually having them.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves artistic stories about love and longing.
